tweets.text:
I had a similar experience with my first big FTX run in the Spring of 2021.

Ran up an account with $30K in it to $12.5M in two and a half weeks.

It's easy to say "why didn't you just walk away", but at the point where you've already done a 400x+ in that short of a time window, you start to think "well, what's another 10x from here?"

And then, when you are down 80-90% and you're sitting in the low millions, you really do think "well, there's no way the market keeps moving against me like this, right? things have to turn back around!"

And they eventually did. Right after I got wiped out.

Part of it can be attributed toward the social side of sharing positions and sharing your journey with others along the way.

The other part is how difficult it is to grasp the reality of the situation, because if this guy is anything like where I was, he's probably left most of the chips on the table.

He hasn't experienced how life changing that money can be.

Best bit of advice to him would be to take what's left, cash out and take a few weeks or months and just completely unplug from the game and reset.

Then put a *portion* back in and leave the rest out and change your life with it.

The biggest issue most people struggle with in this situation is making decisions with what they *had*, rather than focusing on optimizing their strategy for what they have now.

tweets.text:
Just by looking at the chart you would think that $SKHY is bankrupt, but it's actually one of the most profitable companies in the world with record revenue and a positive demand outlook. 

I think that what we're seeing with the Korean stock market is the result of a liquidation cascade similar to the infamous October 10 event that we had in crypto. 

The Koreans stock market was jacked to the tits leveraged long on an index of which its weighting was comprised for 60% of only 2 companies: Samsung and SK Hynix. The ETF leverage and call options open interest was at an all time high.

SK's stock market had become the 6th largest in the world after a monstrous run of +120% since January. Then the market started running on fumes because who was left to buy? Combine that with some CAPEX fears, AI bubble fears that start brewing and a shit ton of leverage and... 

On July 13 there's an epic liquidation cascade where the circuit breaker hits and  1.2 million Korean retail accounts get blown up. Just like with crypto's Oct 10 event, this isn't something that the market can quickly recover from.

As two cherries on top the Bank of Korea raises the interest rate for the first time in three years, and it becomes clear that China's AI & semicon companies are better competition than previously thought. Thus we're seeing an epic crash that the KOSPI hasn't experienced since the Covid crash. 

Today the Korean government held an emergency meeting to discuss if they should do an intervention.

But the funny thing is that this isn't because of major fundamental issues. In fact Samsumg and SK Hynix are still printing phenomenal numbers all in the midst of a tech revolution.

This is the result of forced selling, not collapsing fundamentals.
